# Test plan

<!-- generated by scripts/project_map/build.py from scripts/project_map/annotations.yaml (plan: and tests:) -- edit the YAML and run `make map`; do not edit this file -->

[Open the Test plan view of the project map →](project-map.md#view=plan){ .pm-link }

A verification plan links every **feature** of the DUT to the **stimulus** that exercises it, the **checker** that judges it and the **coverage** that proves it happened. This plan follows the pages of the course's DUT description (packet format, input and output protocols, registers, drop rules, counters, memories, host port) and the lab chapters that add requirements of their own (scoreboard, functional coverage, register tests). **11 feature groups, 56 items**: 55 <span class="st st-covered">covered</span>, 1 <span class="st st-excluded">excluded</span>.

Every item says what is driven, what is checked and by which test; a *partial* item is exercised but not fully checked, a *gap* has no test yet (the note says what one would do), an *excluded* item is left out on purpose. The same data drives the **Test plan** view of the [project map](project-map.md), where every test card lists the items it verifies.

## Features

### ROUTE — Routing

One input port, three output channels: the address in the header picks the channel and the packet comes out unchanged. *Project Overview p. 5 -- YAPP Router Description.* [Read the specification →](dut/spec.md) [On the map →](project-map.md#view=plan&node=plan:ROUTE)

| Item | What is verified, and how | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| **ROUTE-01**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **The address selects the output channel**<br>*Stimulus:* Packets to addresses 0, 1 and 2 (yapp_012_seq, random sequences, yapp_boundary_seq).<br>*Check:* Each channel monitor raises UVM_ERROR when a packet with another address appears on its channel; the scoreboard keeps one expected queue per channel.<br>*Coverage:* `addr_cp.legal (yapp_pkt_cg)` | `yapp_012_test`<br>`simple_test`<br>`router_simple_mcseq_test`<br>`reg_function_test`<br>`router_filter_test` |
| **ROUTE-02**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Payload and parity arrive unchanged**<br>*Stimulus:* Every packet that is forwarded.<br>*Check:* comp_equal() in the scoreboard: address, length, every payload byte and the parity byte of the channel packet equal the YAPP packet; one UVM_ERROR per difference.<br>*Coverage:* `length_cp` | `router_simple_mcseq_test`<br>`scoreboard_drop_test`<br>`coverage_test`<br>`backpressure_test`<br>`router_filter_test` |
| **ROUTE-03**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Order is kept per channel, channels are independent**<br>*Stimulus:* Back-to-back packets to the same channel (0,1,2,0,1,2) and to different channels while the receivers are slow.<br>*Check:* The scoreboard pops its per-channel queue in order: a swapped packet mismatches; the FIFO scoreboard (Lab 9D) blocks on the next packet of that channel. | `router_simple_mcseq_test`<br>`coverage_test`<br>`router_filter_test`<br>`backpressure_test` |
| **ROUTE-04**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Packets back to back with the minimum gap**<br>*Stimulus:* yapp_gap_seq: gaps of 0 (the header in the cycle right after the parity byte -- the shortest the DUT accepts), 1, 2 and 3 cycles; packet_delay is the number of idle cycles. Random traffic keeps 1..20.<br>*Check:* The YAPP monitor counts the idle cycles before every packet; the test compares them with the gaps the sequence asked for. Scoreboard: every packet delivered.<br>*Coverage:* `gap_cp (yapp_gap_cg): back_to_back, one, two, longer` | `back_to_back_test`<br>`coverage_test`<br>`scoreboard_drop_test` |

### PKT — Packet format

Header {length[7:2], addr[1:0]}, 1..63 payload bytes, one even-parity byte over header and payload; address 3 is illegal. *Project Overview p. 6 -- Packet Data Specification.* [Read the specification →](dut/spec.md#packet-format) [On the map →](project-map.md#view=plan&node=plan:PKT)

| Item | What is verified, and how | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| **PKT-01**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Header: length in [7:2], address in [1:0]**<br>*Stimulus:* Every packet; the driver packs {length, addr}, the channel monitor unpacks it again.<br>*Check:* The channel monitor's length and address equal the YAPP packet's (scoreboard compare, channel address check); the DUT reads length + 2 bytes exactly, so the next header is found where the monitor expects it. | `simple_test`<br>`router_simple_mcseq_test`<br>`coverage_test` |
| **PKT-02**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Every payload length 1..63, including both extremes**<br>*Stimulus:* yapp_coverage_seq sends 1, 5, 20, 50 and 63 bytes; random sequences cover the rest; backpressure_test sends 40..63.<br>*Check:* Scoreboard compare; a wrong length would shift the parity byte and the monitors would disagree.<br>*Coverage:* `length_cp bins MIN, SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE, MAX` | `coverage_test`<br>`scoreboard_drop_test`<br>`backpressure_test` |
| **PKT-03**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Address 3 is illegal**<br>*Stimulus:* Packets with addr == 3 (c_addr_legal switched off): yapp_88_packets_seq, yapp_coverage_seq, yapp_boundary_seq.<br>*Check:* No byte appears on any channel (scoreboard: nothing unexpected), the reference model drops it, addr3_cnt_reg counts it when addr3_cnt_en is set.<br>*Coverage:* `addr_cp.illegal_addr` | `test_uvc_integration`<br>`coverage_test`<br>`router_filter_test` |
| **PKT-04**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Even bitwise parity over header and payload**<br>*Stimulus:* Every good packet: parity = XOR of the header and all payload bytes (yapp_packet::calc_parity).<br>*Check:* The channel monitor recomputes the parity and tags the packet CHANNEL_GOOD_PARITY; the DUT counts nothing in parity_err_cnt_reg; no error pulse.<br>*Coverage:* `parity_cp` | `reg_function_test`<br>`coverage_test`<br>`router_filter_test` |
| **PKT-05**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **A wrong parity byte is detected -- and the packet still delivered**<br>*Stimulus:* parity_type == BAD_PARITY flips one bit of the correct parity (yapp_pkt_seq, yapp_coverage_seq, 20 % in yapp_88_packets_seq).<br>*Check:* parity_err_cnt_reg equals the monitor's num_bad_parity; error pulses once per bad packet (error_pulse_checker); the scoreboard still matches the packet (the router forwards it -- see Decisions in dut/spec.md).<br>*Coverage:* `parity_cp, len_x_addr_x_parity (REQ3)` | `reg_function_test`<br>`parity_error_test`<br>`test_uvc_integration` |

### IN — Input port protocol

Driven on the falling edge, sampled on the rising edge; in_data_vld frames header and payload; in_suspend stalls the sender; error pulses 1..10 cycles after a bad packet. *Project Overview p. 7 -- Input Port Protocol.* [Read the specification →](dut/spec.md#input-port-protocol) [On the map →](project-map.md#view=plan&node=plan:IN)

| Item | What is verified, and how | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| **IN-01**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **in_data_vld rises with the header; one byte per falling edge**<br>*Stimulus:* yapp_if.send_to_dut in every packet test.<br>*Check:* DUT, driver and monitor agree on one rule -- a byte is accepted at a rising edge with in_suspend low; a disagreement shows as a parity error or a scoreboard mismatch. | `yapp_012_test`<br>`simple_test`<br>`coverage_test` |
| **IN-02**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **in_data_vld is low with the parity byte**<br>*Stimulus:* Every packet: the driver drops in_data_vld on the falling edge after the last payload byte.<br>*Check:* The DUT's PARITY state takes the next accepted byte regardless of in_data_vld; the monitor samples the parity the same way; the packet count in the DUT (mem_size_reg, counters) matches. | `simple_test`<br>`reg_function_test`<br>`pkt_mem_test` |
| **IN-03**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **in_suspend: the input holds while the target FIFO is full**<br>*Stimulus:* Slow receivers (channel_rx_slow_seq, 20..40 cycles) and 40..63-byte packets, so the 16-byte FIFO fills before the receiver starts.<br>*Check:* in_suspend rose at least once; scoreboard 6 matched, 0 mismatched, 0 unexpected; no parity error at the monitor (every byte accepted exactly once).<br>*Note:* Writing this test showed that yapp_if.wait_accept() sampled in_suspend on the falling edge; it now samples the rising edge, like the DUT and the monitor (see components/driver.md). | `backpressure_test` |
| **IN-04**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **error asserts 1 to 10 cycles after a bad-parity packet**<br>*Stimulus:* 12 packets with bad parity (parity_error_test).<br>*Check:* error_pulse_checker: exactly one pulse per bad packet, 1..10 cycles after the parity byte was accepted; a pulse with no bad packet before it is an error. | `parity_error_test`<br>`test_uvc_integration` |

### OUT — Output port protocol

16-byte FIFO per channel; data_vld_x with the byte, the receiver reads on the falling edge and de-asserts suspend_x; a new byte every rising edge while suspend_x is low. *Project Overview p. 8 -- Output Port Protocol (Channel Ports).* [Read the specification →](dut/spec.md#output-channel-protocol) [On the map →](project-map.md#view=plan&node=plan:OUT)

| Item | What is verified, and how | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| **OUT-01**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **data_vld_x, suspend_x and one byte per rising edge**<br>*Stimulus:* channel_if.receive_packet in every scoreboard test: the receiver reads length + 2 bytes after it drops suspend_x.<br>*Check:* The channel monitor collects exactly length + 2 bytes (a wrong handshake would duplicate or skip a byte and the scoreboard would mismatch); the address check never fires. | `simple_test`<br>`router_simple_mcseq_test`<br>`coverage_test` |
| **OUT-02**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **The receiver may answer late: the header is held**<br>*Stimulus:* channel_rx_resp_seq: response delay 0..10 cycles per packet; channel_rx_slow_seq: 20..40.<br>*Check:* Scoreboard compare: the header read after the delay is still the header. | `simple_test`<br>`router_simple_mcseq_test`<br>`backpressure_test` |
| **OUT-03**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **The FIFO is 16 bytes deep**<br>*Stimulus:* Packets longer than 16 bytes with a receiver that waits 20..40 cycles: the FIFO fills, the router stalls the input.<br>*Check:* in_suspend seen (backpressure_test); no byte lost (scoreboard); the FIFO never overflows (a lost byte would show as a parity error). | `backpressure_test`<br>`scoreboard_drop_test` |
| **OUT-04**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **suspend_x is re-asserted at the parity byte: the next packet waits**<br>*Stimulus:* Back-to-back packets to the same channel (0,1,2,0,1,2 and the boundary sequence).<br>*Check:* The second packet's header is held in the FIFO until the receiver answers again; the scoreboard matches both in order. | `router_simple_mcseq_test`<br>`router_filter_test`<br>`backpressure_test` |
| **OUT-05**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **All three channels busy at the same time**<br>*Stimulus:* Random addresses with slow receivers: packets to channels 0, 1 and 2 are in flight together.<br>*Check:* Scoreboard: every channel matched, nothing unexpected. | `backpressure_test`<br>`coverage_test` |

### REG — Registers

ctrl_reg (maxpktsize) and en_reg are RW, the six counters and mem_size_reg are RO; reset values 0x3f, 0x01 and 0x00. *Project Overview p. 9, Lab 11 p. 49 -- Packet Router DUT Registers.* [Read the specification →](dut/spec.md#registers) [On the map →](project-map.md#view=plan&node=plan:REG)

| Item | What is verified, and how | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| **REG-01**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Reset values**<br>*Stimulus:* uvm_reg_hw_reset_seq reads every register right after reset.<br>*Check:* The built-in sequence compares each read with the model's reset value: ctrl_reg 0x3f, en_reg 0x01, counters and mem_size_reg 0x00. | `uvm_reset_test` |
| **REG-02**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **RW registers: every bit can be written and read back**<br>*Stimulus:* Walking one, walking zero, 0x00, 0xff, 0xaa, 0x55 through ctrl_reg and en_reg (20 patterns each).<br>*Check:* After each write the front-door read and the backdoor peek return the pattern; the reserved bits ctrl_reg[7:6] and en_reg[3] hold their value (they are RW in the router). | `reg_bit_walk_test`<br>`reg_access_test` |
| **REG-03**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **RO registers ignore writes**<br>*Stimulus:* Front-door writes to every counter and to mem_size_reg (register model) and a raw HBUS write to 0x1004.<br>*Check:* peek after the write shows the poked value, the read shows 0x00 after the raw write. | `reg_access_test`<br>`reg_introspection_test`<br>`reg_bit_walk_test`<br>`hbus_protocol_test` |
| **REG-04**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Front door and backdoor see the same flip-flops**<br>*Stimulus:* write -> peek and poke -> read on a RW register; poke -> read on a RO register (-access +rwc).<br>*Check:* The values agree; the HDL paths of the model (hw_top.dut.u_regs.<reg>) resolve. | `reg_access_test`<br>`reg_introspection_test` |
| **REG-05**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Unmapped addresses read 0x00 and ignore writes**<br>*Stimulus:* Write 0xa5 then read 0x1002, 0x1003, 0x1007, 0x1008, 0x100c, 0x100e, 0x100f and 0x1050 with raw HBUS sequences.<br>*Check:* Every read returns 0x00. | `hbus_protocol_test` |
| **REG-06**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **mem_size_reg holds the payload length of the last packet**<br>*Stimulus:* A 20-byte packet, then a 9-byte packet that is dropped as oversized.<br>*Check:* mem_size_reg reads 20, then 9 (only bits [5:0] are used). | `pkt_mem_test` |
| **REG-07**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Automatic checking on read (check_on_read + predict)**<br>*Stimulus:* The reg_function_test stimulus with set_check_on_read(1); predict() loads the expected counter before each read.<br>*Check:* The map compares every read with the mirror and raises UVM_ERROR on a difference. | `reg_function_check_test` |

### DROP — Drop rules

The whole packet is dropped when length > maxpktsize, when the router is disabled, or when the address is 3; changing the enables mid-packet is undefined. *Project Overview p. 10 -- maxpktsize, router_en, counters.* [Read the specification →](dut/spec.md#behaviour-rules) [On the map →](project-map.md#view=plan&node=plan:DROP)

| Item | What is verified, and how | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| **DROP-01**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **length > maxpktsize drops the whole packet**<br>*Stimulus:* maxpktsize = 20 with full-size packets (scoreboard_drop_test, test_uvc_integration); maxpktsize = 10 with lengths 9, 10, 11 and 63 (router_filter_test).<br>*Check:* Nothing of the packet appears on the channel: the reference model drops it and the scoreboard sees nothing unexpected; `ROUTER DROPS PACKET ... length > maxpktsize`; length == maxpktsize still passes. | `router_filter_test`<br>`scoreboard_drop_test`<br>`test_uvc_integration` |
| **DROP-02**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **router_en = 0 drops every packet**<br>*Stimulus:* en_reg = 0xfe, then yapp_012_seq; en_reg = 0xff, yapp_012_seq again.<br>*Check:* Channel monitors collect nothing while disabled, the reference model reports 3 dropped (router disabled), no counter and not mem_size_reg moves; after re-enabling the packets flow and the address counters read 1. | `router_disable_test` |
| **DROP-03**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Address 3 drops the packet**<br>*Stimulus:* As PKT-03.<br>*Check:* Reference model drop, no unexpected channel packet, `ROUTER DROPS PACKET ... illegal address`. | `router_filter_test`<br>`coverage_test`<br>`test_uvc_integration` |
| **DROP-04**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **An oversized packet to address 3 counts in both counters**<br>*Stimulus:* The 11- and 63-byte packets to address 3 of yapp_boundary_seq.<br>*Check:* oversized_pkt_cnt_reg counts them and addr3_cnt_reg counts them (the DUT evaluates the conditions independently -- see Decisions in dut/spec.md). | `router_filter_test` |
| **DROP-05**<br><span class="st st-excluded">excluded</span> | **Changing router_en or a counter enable in the middle of a packet**<br>*Note:* The specification declares the behaviour undefined, so no test drives it; every test programs the registers between packets. | — |

### CNT — Counters

Six 8-bit counters, each behind an enable bit of en_reg: parity errors, oversized packets, and one per address including the illegal 3. *Project Overview p. 10 -- The router counters.* [Read the specification →](dut/spec.md#registers) [On the map →](project-map.md#view=plan&node=plan:CNT)

| Item | What is verified, and how | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| **CNT-01**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **A counter counts only while its enable bit is set**<br>*Stimulus:* en_reg = 0x01 then 0xff around yapp_012_seq (address counters); 0xff then 0x01 around yapp_boundary_seq (oversized, addr3, addrN); 0x03 then 0x01 around bad packets (parity).<br>*Check:* The counters read 0 (or stay frozen) while disabled and the exact packet count while enabled. | `reg_function_test`<br>`router_filter_test`<br>`parity_error_test` |
| **CNT-02**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **addrN_cnt_reg counts every received packet with address N**<br>*Stimulus:* yapp_boundary_seq: 4 packets per address, half of them dropped as oversized.<br>*Check:* addr0/1/2_cnt_reg read 4 each: dropped packets are counted too (they were received -- see Decisions); yapp_012_seq twice gives 2 each. | `router_filter_test`<br>`reg_function_test` |
| **CNT-03**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **parity_err_cnt_reg counts the bad-parity packets**<br>*Stimulus:* yapp_012_seq twice (random parity) and 8 + 4 deliberately bad packets.<br>*Check:* The register equals the YAPP monitor's num_bad_parity delta, then 8, then still 8 with the enable off. | `reg_function_test`<br>`parity_error_test` |
| **CNT-04**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **oversized_pkt_cnt_reg counts packets longer than maxpktsize**<br>*Stimulus:* 8 oversized packets of yapp_boundary_seq (11 and 63 bytes against maxpktsize 10); none in reg_function_test (maxpktsize 63).<br>*Check:* Reads 8, then 0 in reg_function_test. | `router_filter_test`<br>`reg_function_test` |
| **CNT-05**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **addr3_cnt_reg counts packets to address 3**<br>*Stimulus:* 4 packets to address 3 (yapp_boundary_seq); none in yapp_012_seq.<br>*Check:* Reads 4, and 0 in reg_function_test. | `router_filter_test`<br>`reg_function_test` |
| **CNT-06**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Counter overflow after 255 packets**<br>*Stimulus:* 257 one-byte packets to address 0 with every counter enabled.<br>*Check:* addr0_cnt_reg reads 255 after 255 packets, 0 after the 256th (it wraps, it does not saturate), 1 after the 257th.<br>*Note:* The specification is silent; wrapping is the decision recorded in dut/spec.md. Every counter is the same `+ 8'd1` in yapp_hbus_regs, so one counter stands for all six. | `counter_wrap_test` |

### MEM — Memories

yapp_pkt_mem (64 bytes, RO) holds the last packet received; yapp_mem (256 bytes, RW) is scratch memory. *Project Overview p. 10, Lab 11 p. 50 -- Router Memories.* [Read the specification →](dut/spec.md#memories) [On the map →](project-map.md#view=plan&node=plan:MEM)

| Item | What is verified, and how | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| **MEM-01**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **yapp_pkt_mem holds the last packet, byte by byte**<br>*Stimulus:* A 20-byte packet to address 1 whose content the sequence keeps in req.<br>*Check:* yapp_pkt_mem[0] == {length, addr}, yapp_pkt_mem[1..20] == payload[0..19], read through the register model. | `pkt_mem_test` |
| **MEM-02**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **yapp_pkt_mem is read-only**<br>*Stimulus:* A raw HBUS write to 0x1010 with the inverted header.<br>*Check:* yapp_pkt_mem[0] still reads the header. | `pkt_mem_test` |
| **MEM-03**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **A dropped packet is still stored**<br>*Stimulus:* maxpktsize = 5 and a 9-byte packet.<br>*Check:* mem_size_reg reads 9 and the bytes are in yapp_pkt_mem: the packet was received, just not forwarded (Decisions in dut/spec.md). | `pkt_mem_test` |
| **MEM-04**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **yapp_mem: every byte can be written and read back**<br>*Stimulus:* uvm_mem_walk_seq: writes and reads the 256 bytes with a walking pattern; with +define+INJECT_ERROR the RTL flips bit 3 of address 0x2a.<br>*Check:* The built-in sequence compares; 0 errors without the define, one UVM_ERROR with it (yapp_mem[42]). The regression runs both builds; the second one passes only if the error is reported. | `uvm_mem_walk_test` |

### HBUS — Host port (HBUS)

One-cycle writes and two-cycle reads driven on the falling edge; hdata is bidirectional and tri-stated by the DUT when hen is low. *Project Overview p. 11 -- Host Interface Port Protocol.* [Read the specification →](dut/spec.md#hbus-host-protocol) [On the map →](project-map.md#view=plan&node=plan:HBUS)

| Item | What is verified, and how | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| **HBUS-01**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Write: hen and hwr_rd for one cycle, data latched on the rising edge**<br>*Stimulus:* Every register write (hbus_if.hbus_write): raw sequences and the register model's front door.<br>*Check:* The value is read back (hbus_protocol_test, every reg test); the HBUS monitor decodes one WRITE per access. | `hbus_protocol_test`<br>`router_simple_mcseq_test`<br>`reg_access_test` |
| **HBUS-02**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Read: haddr sampled in cycle 1, hdata driven by the DUT in cycle 2**<br>*Stimulus:* Every register read (hbus_if.hbus_read); hbus_read_max_pkt_seq after each maxpktsize write.<br>*Check:* The value read equals what was written or poked (20 and 63 in router_simple_mcseq_test, 0x2a in hbus_protocol_test); the monitor decodes one READ. | `hbus_protocol_test`<br>`router_simple_mcseq_test`<br>`reg_access_test` |
| **HBUS-03**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **hdata is tri-stated when hen drops**<br>*Stimulus:* A read, then two idle cycles.<br>*Check:* hbus_if.hdata_w reads 'z (the master's output enable is off, so only the DUT could still drive it). | `hbus_protocol_test` |
| **HBUS-04**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Back-to-back accesses**<br>*Stimulus:* uvm_mem_walk_seq (511 writes and 255 reads with no gap), the 20-pattern walks of reg_bit_walk_test.<br>*Check:* Every read returns the expected value; the monitor count equals the number of accesses. | `uvm_mem_walk_test`<br>`reg_bit_walk_test` |
| **HBUS-05**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **The register model's front door is HBUS traffic**<br>*Stimulus:* write()/read() through yapp_rm.default_map and the hbus_reg_adapter.<br>*Check:* The HBUS monitor logs the cycles, and the reference model mirrors maxpktsize and router_en from them (the drop rules follow the model's writes in router_disable_test and router_filter_test). | `reg_function_test`<br>`router_disable_test`<br>`router_filter_test` |

### COV — Functional coverage

The coverage model in yapp_tx_monitor: length buckets, every address including the illegal one, and every length to every legal address with bad parity. *Lab 10 p. 47 -- REQ1, REQ2, REQ3.* [The lab →](labs/lab10.md) [On the map →](project-map.md#view=plan&node=plan:COV)

| Item | What is verified, and how | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| **COV-01**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **REQ1: all packet lengths, bucketed**<br>*Stimulus:* yapp_coverage_seq: 1, 5, 20, 50, 63.<br>*Check:* length_cp bins MIN, SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE, MAX all hit; the monitor report prints 100 %.<br>*Coverage:* `length_cp` | `coverage_test` |
| **COV-02**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **REQ2: every address received a packet, including the illegal one**<br>*Stimulus:* yapp_coverage_seq: addresses 0..3.<br>*Check:* addr_cp bins legal[0..2] and illegal_addr hit.<br>*Coverage:* `addr_cp` | `coverage_test` |
| **COV-03**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **REQ3: every length bucket to every legal address with a parity error**<br>*Stimulus:* yapp_coverage_seq: each length with BAD_PARITY to addresses 0..2.<br>*Check:* The cross len_x_addr_x_parity (good parity and address 3 ignored) reaches 15 of 15 bins.<br>*Coverage:* `len_x_addr_x_parity` | `coverage_test` |

### TB — Testbench mechanics

What the lab tests prove about the environment itself: topology, factory, configuration, sequences, virtual interfaces, the virtual sequencer and the scoreboard. *Labs 2-9 -- the course's own tests.* [The lab →](labs/index.md) [On the map →](project-map.md#view=plan&node=plan:TB)

| Item | What is verified, and how | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| **TB-01**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **The test builds the testbench and the run ends cleanly**<br>*Stimulus:* base_test alone: no sequence, drain time 200 ns.<br>*Check:* print_topology shows uvm_test_top with router_tb below; UVM_ERROR : 0; check_config_usage reports nothing unused. | `base_test` |
| **TB-02**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **A factory type override replaces the packet type everywhere**<br>*Stimulus:* set_type_override_by_type(yapp_packet, short_yapp_packet) before the environment is built.<br>*Check:* Every printed packet is a short_yapp_packet with length < 15; the sequences were not touched. | `short_packet_test`<br>`incr_payload_test`<br>`exhaustive_seq_test`<br>`simple_test`<br>`router_simple_mcseq_test` |
| **TB-03**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **Configuration through the database, checked for use**<br>*Stimulus:* is_active = UVM_PASSIVE on the YAPP agent; configure_sequences() overridden to set nothing.<br>*Check:* The topology has no driver and no sequencer under the agent; no `never used` configuration report. | `set_config_test` |
| **TB-04**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **The sequence library: sub-sequences and post_randomize shaping**<br>*Stimulus:* yapp_exhaustive_seq starts every library sequence once; yapp_incr_payload_seq rewrites the payload to 0 1 2 ...<br>*Check:* One `Executing` line per sequence, the expected packet counts, the incrementing payload. | `exhaustive_seq_test`<br>`incr_payload_test` |
| **TB-05**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **The virtual interface connects the driver to the DUT**<br>*Stimulus:* yapp_012_seq through yapp_if into hw_top.dut.<br>*Check:* Each packet appears on data_0, data_1, data_2 in the waveform; later the channel monitors confirm it. | `yapp_012_test`<br>`simple_test` |
| **TB-06**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **A multichannel sequence coordinates HBUS and YAPP**<br>*Stimulus:* router_simple_mcseq on the virtual sequencer: program, read back, send, reprogram, send.<br>*Check:* The log shows the sub-sequences in order; the read-backs return 20 and 63. | `router_simple_mcseq_test` |
| **TB-07**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **The scoreboard notices a wrong packet**<br>*Stimulus:* Full-size packets while maxpktsize is 20, without the reference model (Lab 9A).<br>*Check:* Expected PKT_COMPARE errors and packets left in the queues: the negative test of the checker itself. | `scoreboard_drop_test` |
| **TB-08**<br><span class="st st-covered">covered</span> | **The register model describes itself**<br>*Stimulus:* get_registers() and find() by get_rights().<br>*Check:* 2 RW and 7 RO registers listed, then the access checks run on all of them. | `reg_introspection_test` |

## Tests

Every test extends `base_test` and only changes what runs. The lab is where the test was born; the test-plan tests exist only in `yapp_project/tb/tests`. Run one with `make run-project TEST=<name>` (or `make run LAB=<lab> TEST=<name>` for a lab).

| Test | Lab | Purpose | Verifies |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base_test` | [2](labs/lab02.md) | The skeleton every test extends: builds router_tb, keeps the run alive 200 ns after the last objection, reports unused settings. | TB-01 |
| `set_config_test` | [4](labs/lab04.md) | Lab 4: a passive agent through the configuration database -- and why the sequence setting lives in a virtual function. | TB-03 |
| `short_packet_test` | [4](labs/lab04.md) | Lab 4: the factory override in action -- the sequence asks for yapp_packet and gets short_yapp_packet. | TB-02 |
| `exhaustive_seq_test` | [5](labs/lab05.md) | Lab 5: one sequence that runs every sequence of the library once (sequences starting sub-sequences). | TB-02, TB-04 |
| `incr_payload_test` | [5](labs/lab05.md) | Lab 5: a sequence that shapes the payload after randomisation. | TB-02, TB-04 |
| `yapp_012_test` | [6](labs/lab06.md) | Lab 6: the first packets into the real DUT -- one per channel, so the connection is easy to check in the waveform. | ROUTE-01, IN-01, TB-05 |
| `simple_test` | [7](labs/lab07.md) | Lab 7: every UVC talking to the DUT with the default sequences only. | ROUTE-01, PKT-01, IN-01, IN-02, OUT-01, OUT-02, TB-02, TB-05 |
| `test_uvc_integration` | [7](labs/lab07.md) | Lab 7: 88 packets of every length and address against a router programmed for small packets. | PKT-03, PKT-05, IN-04, DROP-01, DROP-03 |
| `router_simple_mcseq_test` | [8](labs/lab08.md) | Lab 8: one multichannel sequence on the virtual sequencer programs the router and sends the packets in order. | ROUTE-01, ROUTE-02, ROUTE-03, PKT-01, OUT-01, OUT-02, OUT-04, HBUS-01, HBUS-02, TB-02, TB-06 |
| `scoreboard_drop_test` | [9A](labs/lab09a.md) | Lab 9A: the negative check -- full-size packets while maxpktsize is 20, so the router drops some and the scoreboard must notice. | ROUTE-02, ROUTE-04, PKT-02, OUT-03, DROP-01, TB-07 |
| `coverage_test` | [10](labs/lab10.md) | Lab 10: stimulus written to close the functional coverage model of the YAPP monitor. | ROUTE-02, ROUTE-03, ROUTE-04, PKT-01, PKT-02, PKT-03, PKT-04, IN-01, OUT-01, OUT-05, DROP-03, COV-01, COV-02, COV-03 |
| `uvm_mem_walk_test` | [11B](labs/lab11b.md) | Lab 11B: the built-in memory sequence walks yapp_mem; the RO yapp_pkt_mem is skipped. | MEM-04, HBUS-04 |
| `uvm_reset_test` | [11B](labs/lab11b.md) | Lab 11B: the built-in register sequence that reads every register after reset. | REG-01 |
| `reg_access_test` | [11C](labs/lab11c.md) | Lab 11C: hand-written front-door and backdoor checks on one RW and one RO register. | REG-02, REG-03, REG-04, HBUS-01, HBUS-02 |
| `reg_function_check_test` | [11C](labs/lab11c.md) | Lab 11C (optional): the same test with the model checking every read itself. | REG-07 |
| `reg_function_test` | [11C](labs/lab11c.md) | Lab 11C: do the enable bits and the counters behave? Packets in, counters read through the model. | ROUTE-01, PKT-04, PKT-05, IN-02, CNT-01, CNT-02, CNT-03, CNT-04, CNT-05, HBUS-05 |
| `reg_introspection_test` | [11C](labs/lab11c.md) | Lab 11C (optional): the model tells the test which registers are RW and which are RO, then every one is checked. | REG-03, REG-04, TB-08 |
| `back_to_back_test` | test plan | Test plan: the input port with the shortest gap -- a header in the cycle right after the parity byte -- and gaps of 1, 2 and 3 cycles. | ROUTE-04 |
| `backpressure_test` | test plan | Test plan: the YAPP handshake under back-pressure -- slow receivers fill the 16-byte channel FIFOs, the router stalls the input with in_suspend and no byte is lost. | ROUTE-02, ROUTE-03, PKT-02, IN-03, OUT-02, OUT-03, OUT-04, OUT-05 |
| `counter_wrap_test` | test plan | Test plan: an 8-bit counter wraps from 255 to 0 -- the specification is silent, the Decisions of dut/spec.md fix the choice. | CNT-06 |
| `hbus_protocol_test` | test plan | Test plan: the host port on the wire -- one-cycle writes, two-cycle reads, tri-state after the access, unmapped addresses -- with raw HBUS sequences, no register model. | REG-03, REG-05, HBUS-01, HBUS-02, HBUS-03 |
| `parity_error_test` | test plan | Test plan: what a wrong parity byte does -- the counter counts it (when enabled), error pulses 1..10 cycles later, and the packet is still delivered. | PKT-05, IN-04, CNT-01, CNT-03 |
| `pkt_mem_test` | test plan | Test plan: the packet memory and mem_size_reg hold the last packet, byte by byte, even when the packet was dropped. | IN-02, REG-06, MEM-01, MEM-02, MEM-03 |
| `reg_bit_walk_test` | test plan | Test plan: every bit of every register obeys its policy -- walking ones and zeros through the RW registers, writes ignored by the RO ones. | REG-02, REG-03, HBUS-04 |
| `router_disable_test` | test plan | Test plan: router_en = 0 makes the router deaf -- nothing reaches a channel, nothing is counted, nothing is stored; traffic resumes when it is enabled again. | DROP-02, HBUS-05 |
| `router_filter_test` | test plan | Test plan: the drop rules around the maxpktsize limit and the counters behind them, with the counters enabled and then disabled. | ROUTE-01, ROUTE-02, ROUTE-03, PKT-03, PKT-04, OUT-04, DROP-01, DROP-03, DROP-04, CNT-01, CNT-02, CNT-04, CNT-05, HBUS-05 |

## Writing a new test — checklist

1. Extend `base_test` (or `reg_function_test` when you need the register block, the YAPP sequencer and `check_counter()`); add `` `uvm_component_utils `` and the constructor.
2. Decide the packet type: factory override in `build_phase` *before* `super.build_phase(phase)`.
3. `configure_sequences()`: which sequencer runs what. Always `set_clock_and_channel_sequences()` in Labs 7+ (or your own channel sequence, as `backpressure_test` does).
4. For register tests: get handles in `connect_phase`, raise an objection in `run_phase`, use the model API.
5. Decide what *passes*: `UVM_ERROR : 0` plus the counts in the reports, and say so in the log (`uvm_info` at `UVM_NONE`).
6. Add the test to `annotations.yaml`: a line under `classes:`, its plan under `tests:`, and the items it verifies under `plan:`; `make map` regenerates this page and the map.
